title: Starship Flight 15 / Starlink Group 31-2 (OLP-2, Starbase)
t0_note: SpaceX Flight 15 page: 75-minute window opens 4:45 p.m. CT = 2026-11-13T22:45:00Z, pending regulatory approval. LL2 id 0f867f0c-5422-4d44-93b8-d7faaae7019b, status To Be Confirmed, window 22:45Z–00:00Z (checked 2026-11-11).

Non-rotating i ~31.01 deg. MKJK A0455/26 (further downrange Jamaica FIR debris area) centroid bearing 107.40 deg / i~30.94. Geometric azimuth for 30.5 deg from this pad is 106.54 deg. payload_kg.note: FITTED within 20–80 t so the published 489 s ship ascent cutoff delivers the ASSUMED pre-insertion transfer. 26 Starlink V3 mass unpublished; result is NOT an estimate of the real stack.

insertion_alt_km.assumption: SpaceX publishes ~275 km as the orbital altitude after the T+26:10 insertion burn, not the T+08:09 ascent cutoff. Flight 14 (same 26-sat profile) used a passively safe trajectory, then a short insertion burn. 180 × 275 km is a labelled pre-insertion transfer stand-in (apogee = the published ~275 km; perigee ASSUMED 180 km) so the 20 s insertion burn can raise perigee. Tuned if needed.

apoapsis_alt_km.note: SpaceX: 'orbit the Earth at an altitude of ~275 km and complete approximately 14 orbits ... more than 22-hour flight'.

header_notes: PRE-FLIGHT ILLUSTRATIVE. Starship Flight 15 / Starlink Group 31-2, 26 V3 sats, OLP-2 Starbase, T0 2026-11-13T22:45:00Z (Fri Nov 13 2:45 p.m. PST), 75-minute window, LL2 TBC pending regulatory approval. First attempt to catch both Super Heavy V3 and the ship at the launch site.

Ascent event times are SpaceX's published F15 timeline (MECO 139 s, hot-stage 141 s, ship cutoff 489 s). The 20 s orbital insertion burn (26:10–26:30) is flown post-cutoff; payload deploy start 35:01, complete 1:17:40. Ship is then scheduled to fly ~14 orbits and attempt RTLS catch (deorbit T+21:35:57) — deorbit/catch are not in this file, which ends at deploy complete.

burns.name: Orbital insertion burn

t_ign_s.src: https://www.spacex.com/launches/starship-flight-15 Starship orbital insertion burn start T+00:26:10

duration_s.derived: SpaceX publishes a 20 s insertion (T+00:26:10–26:30). Under the constant 1,600 tf / 350 s Isp ascent assumption the 348 s ship burn leaves only 9143 kg residual, enough for 12.80 s at 1×250 tf (mdot 714.3 kg/s). The burn is flown for this residual-limited duration, not the published 20 s. 1,600 tf is SpaceX “initial thrust”; a constant-thrust model slightly over-burns the 1,600 t load (a 0.24% lower mean mdot would have left a 20 s reserve). Do not invent extra propellant.

thrust_N.assumption: F15 does not state how many engines restart. Flight 14 (same 26-sat profile) used a single sea-level Raptor for insertion. 1 × Raptor 3 SL at 250 tf (2,451,663 N) is the F14 analog, labelled ASSUMPTION.

burns.basis: Open-loop: ASSUMED single Raptor 3 SL (2,451,663 N, F14 analog) for the residual-limited duration 12.80 s (published 20 s cannot be completed: constant 1,600 tf / 350 s leaves only 9143 kg). Not solved to a perigee target. The impulse still exceeds a 180×275 km circularization (~26 m/s); residuals are reported, not hidden.

deploy.src: SpaceX Flight 15 timeline: deploy start T+00:35:01, complete T+01:17:40
deploy.label: Starlink V3 deploy complete (26 sats)

notes: SpaceX target altitude ~275 km after the insertion burn. A 20 s / 1×250 tf burn is ~236 m/s at this cutoff mass, vs ~26 m/s to circularize a 180×275 km transfer; the residual-limited ~13 s burn is still ~150 m/s. The resulting orbit is not expected to be 275 km circular. Residuals are reported, not hidden.

Ship residual propellant after a constant 1,600 tf / 350 s, 348 s ascent is 9.14 t, short of the 14.3 t a published 20 s insertion would need. Insertion is flown residual-limited. 1,600 tf is published as initial thrust (SpaceX via Wikipedia).
Deorbit burn T+21:35:57 and ship catch T+22:32:34 (SpaceX F15 timeline) are not modelled; file ends at deploy complete T+01:17:40.

fitted.method: scipy least_squares (TRF, bounded) vs published knots + target orbit

payload_kg.basis: 26 Starlink V3 satellites, mass unpublished by SpaceX. NSF unofficial 44–52 t is NOT used as a source. Fitted payload is NOT an estimate of the real stack.
